notes: Ground truth for deterministic lab scenarios. Clean point is BKP-007: compromise window opens 90 minutes before detection while snapshots are hourly, so BKP-008 (taken inside/after the window) carries malicious markers in BOTH scenarios. In corrupted_latest, BKP-008 additionally fails checksum verification. Recovery order = tier-ascending topological order with alphabetical tie-break (config-store and object-storage have no dependencies; core-postgres requires config-store, etc.).

standard.description: Ransomware mass-encryption at T0-90m; hourly backup history; latest snapshot taken inside compromise window.

corrupted_latest.description: Same as standard plus the LATEST backup's manifest is tampered so its checksum no longer verifies; naive latest restore would reintroduce corruption.
